abstract.p: Procedural text adaptation-such as modifying recipes or revising instructional guides-has traditionally relied on specialized models extensively fine-tuned for specific domains. To address the scalability limitations of such approaches, recent research has increasingly turned to general-purpose large language models (LLMs). However, existing prompting strategies for LLMs often yield superficial or erroneous adaptations due to alignment-induced biases and the inherent complexity of procedural editing. To overcome these challenges, we propose the Over-generation-and-Compaction (OC) prompting strategy, which first elicits diverse procedural details to leverage the model's latent knowledge, and subsequently compacts them into concise, coherent adaptations. We further introduce Recipe Consistency & Feasibility (RCF), a novel metric for systematically evaluating the procedural validity and practical feasibility of recipe adaptations. Experiments on public datasets show that OC substantially enhances adaptation consistency and feasibility over baseline prompting methods, without requiring additional fine-tuning or curated training resources.
